artifacts.name: test_why_section_pairs_four_problems_with_their_answers
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor reads the Why section to learn what MAID prevents.

expected.behavior: The Why section leads with governing the artifacts agents produce and holds exactly four problem cards in order: Plan drift, Test rewriting, Self-reported "done", and Rules that live in one tool. Each names MAID's answer: a plan lock an agent can't quietly rewrite plus declared files; failing tests first plus Python-only, opt-in knockout; verification plus independent review; and a deterministic, AST-level manifest contract that runs the same under Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Windsurf.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_states_each_differentiator_in_one_place
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor scrolls the homepage without meeting the same claim three times.

expected.behavior: The separate Strengths band and Capabilities section, their card classes, the Capabilities anchor, and all eight retired duplicate card titles are gone, and the knockout, plan-lock, and independent-review claims each appear exactly once.

artifacts.name: test_navigation_and_sections_put_quick_start_after_the_workflow
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor ready to install looks for Quick start right after learning the workflow.

expected.behavior: The primary navigation links exactly why-maid, workflow, quickstart, and maid-in-practice in that order, the sections appear in the same order, and the final CTA follows them.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_matches_mockup_story_and_navigation
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor opens the canonical MAID Runner homepage and scans the product story.

expected.behavior: The homepage exposes the hero, primary actions, navigation anchors for Why MAID Runner, Workflow, Quick start, and MAID in practice, validation panels, the Plan drift and Test rewriting problems, and semantic page sections.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_leads_with_core_strengths
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor scans the Why section for MAID Runner's differentiated value.

expected.behavior: The page leads with governing the artifacts agents produce and states each differentiator once as MAID's answer: an approved plan lock as the contract, tests that must fail before the change, verification plus independent review before handoff, and a manifest contract that runs the same under any agent.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_renders_workflow_capabilities_tools_and_quickstart
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor scrolls through the homepage to understand the MAID loop and how to start.

expected.behavior: The page renders the seven-step plan-to-evidence workflow, tool compatibility, and the supported quick-start commands without suggesting maid verify on an empty repository.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_renders_maid_in_practice_section
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor looks for evidence that MAID is used on real software.

expected.behavior: The practice section renders JSON-mirrored public stats, private-production language, and inspectable project links without unsupported ecosystem claims.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_uses_final_local_brand_and_social_assets
artifacts.source_scenario: A browser or social crawler loads the canonical homepage assets.

expected.behavior: All local asset references resolve to final PNG assets and disposable design inputs remain absent.

artifacts.name: test_mobile_navigation_covers_javascript_and_no_javascript_paths
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor uses compact navigation with JavaScript enabled or disabled.

expected.behavior: Navigation supports open, close, link dismissal, Escape dismissal, focus return, and a usable no-JavaScript fallback.

artifacts.name: test_dark_surface_accessibility_contract_is_declared
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor reads and navigates the dark site across desktop and mobile.

expected.behavior: The stylesheet retains readable tokens, visible focus states, responsive rules, and reduced-motion handling.

artifacts.name: test_static_fallback_and_search_metadata_target_canonical_domain
artifacts.source_scenario: A crawler reads canonical metadata, robots policy, and the sitemap.

expected.behavior: The fallback links home, robots points to the HTTPS apex sitemap, and the homepage canonical plus sitemap locations contain only https://maidrunner.dev/.

artifacts.name: test_vercel_is_the_only_declared_website_deployment
artifacts.source_scenario: A website change is deployed and a maintainer audits the repository's hosting contract.

expected.behavior: Root vercel.json serves website/ as the output directory; deployment docs distinguish repository automation from external Pages settings; every workflow is free of Pages deployment markers; and crawl surfaces never advertise HTTP or www aliases.

artifacts.name: test_homepage_surfaces_knockout_strength
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor checks whether MAID's tests actually catch bugs rather than just execute lines.

expected.behavior: The test-rewriting answer surfaces differential knockout: deep verification can delete a function's body and require the tests to fail so a gutted test can't pass, disclosed as Python-only and opt-in.

artifacts.name: test_every_html_page_loads_configured_google_analytics_tag
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor loads any HTML page published by Vercel.

expected.behavior: Every shipped HTML page loads gtag.js asynchronously and initializes Google Analytics exactly once inside its head with measurement ID G-B6F335E4MM.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_uses_existing_uv_installs_requested_version_and_verifies_maid
artifacts.source_scenario: A macOS or Linux user already has uv and requests a reproducible MAID Runner version.

expected.behavior: The installer keeps existing uv, installs the requested version with Python 3.12, refreshes PATH, and verifies maid before succeeding.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_bootstraps_uv_when_missing
artifacts.source_scenario: A macOS or Linux user runs the installer without uv.

expected.behavior: The installer retrieves Astral's official uv installer, discovers uv, installs MAID Runner, and verifies the command.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_rejects_unsafe_or_incomplete_arguments
artifacts.source_scenario: A caller supplies an unsafe version, omits a value, or uses an unsupported option.

expected.behavior: The installer exits nonzero with usage guidance before invoking uv.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_propagates_download_and_tool_failures
artifacts.source_scenario: The uv download or MAID Runner installation fails.

expected.behavior: The installer exits nonzero, skips later verification, and never prints success.

artifacts.name: test_powershell_installer_contract_is_auditable_and_fail_closed
artifacts.source_scenario: A reviewer inspects the Windows bootstrapper without PowerShell execution support.

expected.behavior: The script validates versions, uses Astral's HTTPS installer, checks exits, installs with Python 3.12, refreshes PATH, and verifies maid before success.

artifacts.name: test_shell_installer_passes_shellcheck
artifacts.source_scenario: A maintainer validates the POSIX bootstrapper.

expected.behavior: ShellCheck accepts the installer with no diagnostics.

artifacts.name: test_readme_and_landing_page_publish_bootstrap_installers_as_primary
artifacts.source_scenario: A newcomer scans the README or landing page for installation.

expected.behavior: Both surfaces present first-party shell and PowerShell installers before uv and pip alternatives and include first-run commands.

artifacts.name: test_installer_smoke_workflow_runs_local_scripts_on_all_supported_platforms
artifacts.source_scenario: An installer or installer-workflow change is proposed or lands on main.

expected.behavior: A path-scoped workflow executes checked-out shell installers on Ubuntu/macOS and PowerShell on Windows with least-privilege contents access.

artifacts.name: test_no_rendered_text_is_smaller_than_twelve_pixels
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor reads labels, metadata, code, captions, and buttons on the homepage or 404 page at phone, tablet, and desktop widths.

expected.behavior: Every element with its own text on index.html and 404.html computes and renders at 12px or larger, including first-line, first-letter, and generated pseudo-element text, in every declared width, touch, landscape, no-JavaScript, reduced-motion, and open-navigation scenario, including list markers; the stylesheet uses only the pinned conditional groups; and nothing shrinks text through font-size-adjust, small caps, or @font-face size-adjust.

artifacts.name: test_body_copy_renders_at_the_reading_floor
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor reads the explanatory copy that teaches the MAID method in cards and intros.

expected.behavior: Each declared body-copy selector (hero lede, Why-section problem and answer copy, workflow captions, practice copy, quick-start copy, and the 404 paragraph) matches rendered text on its page in every scenario, and all of that text except the problem-answer label renders at 15px or larger.

artifacts.name: test_rendered_tracking_never_tightens_past_the_legibility_floor
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor reads the hero headline "Don't just trust AI code. Verify it." and the section headings.

expected.behavior: No rendered text, including first-line, first-letter, and generated pseudo-element text, on either page has letter-spacing tighter than -0.04 of its computed font size in any scenario.

artifacts.name: test_display_headings_render_with_balanced_wrapping
artifacts.source_scenario: A visitor on any screen width reads the hero and section headlines.

expected.behavior: The hero h1, every section h2, and the final CTA h2 compute text-wrap-style: balance and text-wrap-mode: wrap in every index.html scenario.

artifacts.name: test_maid_runner_ci_installs_chromium_before_running_website_tests
artifacts.source_scenario: CI runs the MAID test contract, the validation gate, or the publish test matrix after this browser test exists.

expected.behavior: maid-test.yml, maid-validation.yml, and publish.yml each run exactly `uv run playwright install --with-deps chromium` before their MAID test or validation step, and the reusable workflows gate it with a step-level github.repository condition or the inline repository guard used by the npm and payload-sync steps.

scope.reason: The Strengths, Why, and Capabilities sections merge into one four-row problem-to-answer Why section; Quick start moves directly after the workflow; navigation drops the Capabilities anchor. Hero, workflow, install card, practice section, final CTA, canonical metadata, and analytics are otherwise preserved.
Strength-card, capability-card, and tools styles are removed or folded into the four-row Why section; the readable type floor, tokens, and existing breakpoints are preserved.
Existing progressive-enhancement navigation remains part of the complete website contract.
Existing static fallback remains part of the complete website contract.
Crawler policy must continue pointing only to the canonical HTTPS apex sitemap.
Search discovery must continue listing only the final 200-status canonical homepage.
The production PNG remains the authoritative brand asset.
The social preview remains part of the website asset contract.
The evidence-backed practice statistics remain the canonical data source for homepage copy.
The existing POSIX bootstrap endpoint remains part of the complete website contract.
The existing PowerShell bootstrap endpoint remains part of the complete website contract.
The existing bootstrap installer onboarding hierarchy remains part of the superseded installer contract.
The cross-platform installer smoke workflow remains active and distinct from website publishing.
Repository-owned Vercel configuration serves the static website/ directory without relying on stale Pages automation.
Deployment documentation records Vercel as the only publisher and explains intentional canonical-domain redirects.
Adds playwright to the dev dependency group for the browser integration test.
Lockfile update for the playwright dev dependency.
Installs Chromium for maid-runner's own MAID test job before the manifest test contract runs; gated so downstream callers are unaffected.
Installs Chromium for maid-runner's own validation gate, whose verify test stage runs manifest validate commands; gated so downstream callers are unaffected.
Installs Chromium in the publish test matrix before MAID tests and the full suite run.
Contributor setup gains the Chromium install step, since pytest, maid test, and the maid-verify hook now run the browser test.

delete.reason: The GitHub Pages publisher is obsolete now that Vercel serves the production domain.
The removed generated logo variant must remain absent.
The disposable design reference must remain absent.
The disposable social-card source variant must remain absent.
